label: recorder
headline: Eight records, D-137 through D-144, written into docs/DECISIONS.md for a release that has NOT happened: nothing was tagged, released, uploaded or committed. The three a reader in a year cannot reconstruct are recorded as their own records -- why 0.4.0 and not 0.3.1 or 1.0.0 (two breaking changes in a 0.x line, and the package split made non-breaking ON PURPOSE by 19 identity-preserving shims), what 0.4.0 ships KNOWN-BROKEN (7 defects, 6 of them on the release notes' first screen and the seventh nowhere in the section), and the one-way door (PyPI holds exactly ['0.3.0'], 0.4.0 answers 404, and D-023's decisive fact -- that PyPI returned 404 for the name -- expired at the first upload with the migration it gated unfinished). One load-bearing claim per workstream was re-derived in a fresh process rather than read. The brief's own arithmetic was killed by the recorder's first falsifier: normalize breaks idempotence on 1050, not 1076. And the unattributed '4 failed, 6183 passed' run one workstream could not explain was REPRODUCED and root-caused: a test writes a real file into docs/ and a concurrent run's rotation tests fail on it.
shipped: docs/DECISIONS.md: 8 records appended as one ASCENDING block, D-137 (the round frame, four re-derivations and the reproduced concurrency mechanism), D-138 (the version decision), D-139 (what 0.4.0 ships known-broken), D-140 (the one-way door, second passage), D-141 (every pre-registration this round wrote), D-142 (the eighth cold read adjudicated), D-143 (the definition of done, eleventh sweep), D-144 (the quota). 136 records to 144, +652 lines and 0 deletions. Every figure in the block is inside a code span or a fenced block, which is why docs/DECISIONS.md's deferred count stays at 42 and the register stays at 185 of 185.

D-138 records the version decision with the half a version number cannot carry: 0.3.1 is excluded by the two breaking changes themselves under SemVer's 0.x clause; 1.0.0 is excluded on this project's own evidence (7 known-open defects, 2 empty headline rows, 0 uncontaminated held-out corpora for either headline task, a 21-of-42 in-situ gate debt); and THE SPLIT WAS MADE NON-BREAKING ON PURPOSE -- 19 of 19 pre-split paths import, object identity holds on all three spot checks, __all__ is unchanged at 49, and only __module__ moved. A later round seeing acronymkit.governed still importable could otherwise conclude the split was never finished.

D-139 assembles the known-broken list in one place because it exists nowhere else as a list: the 26-code-point round trip reporting unaccounted=(), the 1050-wide ordinal class and its interpreter dependence (890/977/1050/1050/1048 across Unicode 13.0 to 16.0, union 1076), A2's withdrawn 5.95x multiple against a +3.07-point scored gain, selective risk's 8-of-18 cells and SDU-21's 17.53 % selection-family floor, both empty headline rows re-derived by running splits.py --check, the unreproducible byte-identity proof -- AND item 7, loaders._read_pairs, which is recorded in the tree and is the one known-open defect the [0.4.0] section does not carry.

D-140 records the one-way door with the tag arithmetic and two asymmetric edges measured rather than assumed: vv0.4.0 PASSES the build assertion because lstrip('v') strips every leading v (PyPI would get 0.4.0 while the release page and the [0.4.0]: footer link sit at a tag that does not exist), and V0.4.0 FAILS because lstrip is case-sensitive, which is the safe direction. It also records that D-023's window closed on 2026-08-11 with the pydantic migration unfinished: pydantic is imported at module top level in 4 of the 65 .py files in the 0.4.0 wheel, and typing_extensions appears in 0 of the 65.

The walk was re-run over all ten files rather than inherited: --classify gives gate-able 52, blocked 129, not-a-claim 4, and the run-id-naming probe re-run over all 185 gives CITABLE 6 with ALL 6 IN CHANGELOG.md, so the payable population is 0 and the sixth waiver is arithmetic.
pre_registration: Six falsifiers, written before the measurements. (1) The ten gates would reproduce the 6d44002 baseline exactly -- HELD, every figure: 6187 passed / 10 skipped / 3 xfailed, value-matched 64 of 64, deferred 185 of 185, in-situ 21 of 42. (2) The brief's '1,076 code points break normalize idempotence' would be wrong -- FIRED. Re-derived exhaustively over all 1,114,112 code points, 2,503,638 verb calls, importing only the library: normalize breaks on 1050, to_physical_name on 1076, the union is 1076, the classes are disjoint and 1050 + 26 = 1076. Publishing the brief's phrasing would have put a wrong number in a release defect list. (3) The payable deferred population would be 0 and every remaining citable number would sit in CHANGELOG.md -- HELD, 6 of 6, and gate-able fell 56 to 52 and CITABLE 9 to 6 by exactly D-136's four payments, so the probe reproduces. (4) At least one brief-named known-open defect would be missing from the release notes -- FIRED: loaders._read_pairs, reproduced independently (5 data rows, 2 unusable, 3 entries, 0 warnings, no member naming the drop). (5) The definition-of-done sweep would move 0 verdicts and hold at 11 of 20 -- HELD, and it is the first time this page's own magnitude prediction has been exact rather than merely the right order. (6) acronymkit.__version__ in this checkout would resolve out of the stale src/acronymkit.egg-info rather than a _FALLBACK_VERSION -- HELD, and it is the falsifier that found what nobody predicted: a real non-editable acronymkit 0.3.0 installed in user site-packages, answering the same import from outside the checkout. NOT PRE-REGISTERED AND THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS ROUND PRODUCED: the unattributed 4-failed suite run has a mechanism, and I hit it by running two pytest processes against one checkout.
how_it_fails: THE ORDERING OF D-139 IS THE PRODUCT AND IT IS A JUDGEMENT NOBODY MEASURED. Seven defects in one record is a wall, and I put the omitted one last, the position a reader reaches least often, for the sole reason that the six above it are what the release notes already say. The argument that item 7 is the worst omission rests on my assertion that loading a CSV is a first-contact path; nobody has measured how many callers reach load_csv, and unlike D-130's 0 of 285,839 the record carries no incidence figure. If that population is small the finding is still true and less urgent than I ranked it. THE DoD SWEEP'S 0 IS THE SAME SHAPE A STALE PAGE HAS. I re-derived 9 of 20 and CARRIED 11, three of them (2, 5, 6) for an eighth consecutive sweep; a verdict not re-derived in eight sweeps is a verdict nobody has tested against the tree that exists. THE QUOTA'S 0 IS UNFALSIFIABLE BY THIS ROUND'S OWN CONSTRUCTION. All 6 remaining citable numbers are in CHANGELOG.md, which I was forbidden to edit, so the round that measured the population at 0 is the round that could not have paid a non-zero one. The measurement is sound and the independence is not. THE FULL SUITE WAS GREEN TWICE AND RED ONCE, AND THE RED WAS MINE. Runs 1 and 2 (hand-off tree, and after every substantive edit) returned 6187 passed / 10 skipped / 3 xfailed rc=0 with the other nine gates rc=0. Run 3 returned 2 failed / 6185 passed because I had a second pytest running against the same checkout: tests/test_check_external.py:340 writes docs/zz-gate-mutation-probe.md and deletes it, and while it exists tests/test_second_reader_policy.py fails two tests on a user-facing document no rotation trigger reaches. Run 4 was abandoned on wall-clock, and KILLING IT LEFT A SECOND PROBE BEHIND -- tests/test_claims_gate_coverage.py's line in README.md asserting a governed-expansion accuracy this project has never measured, in the file PyPI renders. check_claims.py reported it unbacked, README.md was restored from HEAD, and the tree hands off clean; but the honest statement is that the tenth gate's final verdict rests on runs 1 and 2 plus a targeted re-run of every test module that reads the two documents I edited (all rc=0) and the six non-pytest gates re-run green on the final bytes, not on a third full green line. AND THE SITE-PACKAGES FINDING IS A FACT ABOUT THIS MACHINE. A real acronymkit 0.3.0 in user site-packages is why the repo root answers 0.3.0 and src/ on sys.path answers 0.4.0 out of a stale egg-info; neither _FALLBACK_VERSION is reachable here, so the checklist's 0.1.0 cannot be reproduced on this machine at all, and nothing in the ten gates would ever say so because tests/conftest.py:20 inserts src at sys.path[0].
not_done: NOTHING WAS TAGGED, RELEASED, UPLOADED OR COMMITTED. No TestPyPI dry run, no offline bundles, no SPDX SBOM. The version bump and the whole [0.4.0] section are still UNCOMMITTED, and ci.yml triggers on push, pull_request and workflow_dispatch and on NO TAG, so the green tick that matters does not yet exist for the commit that will carry this work.
CHANGELOG.md NOT EDITED, as instructed -- so D-139 item 7 is reported and not fixed. The fix is one bullet in the KNOWN-OPEN block naming loaders._read_pairs, and it is owed before the tag.

The cold read's F-1 is reported upward and not fixed: the [0.4.0] lead says 'Two breaking changes' and 'everything else in this section is additive', while the section carries 6 occurrences of BREAKING across THREE distinct changes (normalize at :19, is_compliant at :30, data_packs removed from the capability report at :143). The section understates what breaks, on its own first screen, by its own labels.

I recorded the mechanism in D-137 and changed no test: a concurrency guard or a session-scoped lock is a test-suite change inside a release commit.
